PRISM stores its researcher accounts, experiments and participant data in a **Firebase** project that you own. This guide walks you through creating that project in the Firebase Console and collecting the details the PRISM installer asks for. Complete it before following the [Setup Guide](developer.qmd), except the last section, [Add the signing fingerprints](#fingerprints), which you do during installation.

By the end of this guide you will have:

- A Firebase project on the pay-as-you-go **Blaze** plan.
- Email/password and Google sign-in turned on.
- A Firestore database and a Cloud Storage bucket, both in Sydney (`australia-southeast1`).
- Firebase Hosting set up.
- A registered **Android app** and its `google-services.json` file.
- A registered **web app** and its **Web API Key** (`apiKey`).

You will need a Google account, plus a payment method or access to an existing Cloud Billing account.

## Data storage and privacy

PRISM collects audio and health data from participants. Most of it is stored in the Firebase project owned by the researcher that you create in this guide, which is hosted by Google. See [Privacy and Security in Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy) and the [Firebase Data Processing and Security Terms](https://firebase.google.com/terms/data-processing-terms) for details.

### What the app uploads

While a recording session is open, the participant's phone records audio continuously. Each time the participant presses a rating button, the app uploads:

- An unprocessed audio clip of up to 30 seconds, ending at the button press.
- Heart-rate variability and skin temperature readings from the previous 30 minutes, if the participant has allowed access to Android Health Connect.
- If a watch is used, an audio clip from the watch, plus its accelerometer, gyroscope, heart-rate and ambient-temperature readings.

PRISM doesn't collect location data, and its apps and Research Portal don't use analytics or crash reporting.

::: {.callout-warning}
The **Upload Raw Audio** and other sensor settings in the Research Portal don't currently change what the app collects; everything listed above is uploaded with every rating.
:::

### Where data is stored

| Where | What's stored |
|---|---|
| **Firebase Authentication** | Researchers' email addresses and password hashes. Participants' Google account email, name and profile photo URL, from signing in to the app with Google. |
| **Cloud Firestore** (database) | Experiment settings. Participants' names, email addresses and invitation status. A record of each uploaded file: rating, sound classification, time, size and the phone's Android device ID. |
| **Cloud Storage** (files) | The uploaded files. File names include the date and time, rating, participant's user ID, experiment ID and Android device ID, but not the participant's name or email address. |
| **Cloud Logging** | Server logs containing participants' user IDs and device IDs, kept for 30 days by default. |
| **Participant's phone** | Audio recorded since the last rating, which stays on the phone after the session ends, and any files that failed to upload. Uploaded files are deleted. Sound classification runs on the phone. |
| **Participant's watch** | Audio clips, which the watch app doesn't currently delete. The watch uploads nothing directly; its data goes via the phone. |
| **Your computer / server host** | Any files you download. If you run PRISM locally, also its credentials, including the service account key, which gives full access to all study data. |
| **Email provider** (Mailgun or Gmail) | Invited participants' email addresses, your invitation text and the experiment link. |
| **Google Forms** (optional) | Whatever your survey asks. PRISM doesn't pass any participant details to the form. |

### Location, security and retention

- **Location:** you choose where Firestore and Cloud Storage keep data when you set them up in Steps 10 and 11 (this guide uses `australia-southeast1`, Sydney), and you can't change it later. Firebase Authentication doesn't offer a choice of location. See [Firebase locations](https://firebase.google.com/docs/projects/locations).
- **Security:** Firestore and Cloud Storage encrypt data in transit and at rest. Anyone with access to your Firebase project or service account key can see all study data, so keep that group small.
- **Retention and withdrawal:** data stays until you delete it. Removing a participant in the Research Portal deletes their uploaded files and records, and deleting an experiment deletes all of its data. Participants' sign-in accounts aren't deleted automatically (delete them under **Authentication** in the Firebase console), and you'll need to delete any downloaded copies yourself. Participants can't delete their data or leave an experiment from the app, so your withdrawal procedure should ask them to contact you.

## Create a Firebase project

### Step 1: Name your project

Open the [Firebase Console](https://console.firebase.google.com/), sign in with your Google account and create a new project.

Enter a **Project name** (this example uses `prism-nat1`). Firebase creates a **project ID** from the name, shown underneath it. The project ID can't be changed later and becomes part of your project's web addresses (e.g. `prism-nat1.web.app`), so click the pencil icon if you'd like to edit it now. Click **Continue**.

![Name your project](images/firebase/01-create-project-name.png)

### Step 2: Skip Gemini in Firebase

Gemini in Firebase is an optional AI assistant for the Firebase Console. PRISM doesn't need it, so turning it on is up to you (this example leaves it off). Click **Continue**.

![Gemini in Firebase is optional](images/firebase/02-create-project-gemini.png)

### Step 3: Turn off Google Analytics

PRISM doesn't use Google Analytics either. Switch off **Enable Google Analytics for this project** (it's on by default) and the **Continue** button changes to **Create project**. Click it, then wait for Firebase to finish creating your project.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Before: Analytics on (default)](images/firebase/03-create-project-analytics-on.png)

![After: Analytics off](images/firebase/04-create-project-analytics-off.png)
:::

## Upgrade to the Blaze plan

New projects start on the free **Spark** plan. PRISM relies on paid Firebase services such as Cloud Functions, so your project must be on the pay-as-you-go **Blaze** plan. Blaze still includes the no-cost quota; you only pay for usage beyond it.

### Step 4: Select the Blaze plan

When your project opens, click **Upgrade** at the bottom of the left-hand menu.

![Your new project, on the Spark plan](images/firebase/05-overview-spark-plan.png)

In the **Firebase pricing plans** dialog, click **Select plan** under **Pay as you go (Blaze plan)**.

![Firebase pricing plans](images/firebase/06-upgrade-pricing-plans.png)

### Step 5: Choose a billing account

Select an existing Cloud Billing account from the list, or click **Create a Cloud Billing account** and follow the prompts to add a payment method. If your organisation manages Google Cloud billing centrally, ask your administrator which account to use.

![Choose a Cloud Billing account](images/firebase/07-upgrade-billing-account.png)

### Step 6: Set a budget alert

Enter a **Budget amount in USD** (this example uses $5) and click **Continue**, or click **Skip this step**.

::: {.callout-note}
A budget doesn't cap your spending. It only emails the billing account's administrators when the project's costs approach or exceed the amount you set.
:::

![Set a billing budget](images/firebase/08-upgrade-billing-budget.png)

### Step 7: Link the billing account

Review the summary and click **Link Cloud Billing account**.

![Link Cloud Billing account](images/firebase/09-upgrade-link-billing.png)

Click **Done** to close the confirmation.

![Plan change completed](images/firebase/10-upgrade-complete.png)

The badge next to your project name now reads **Blaze plan**.

![Your project, now on the Blaze plan](images/firebase/11-overview-blaze-plan.png)

## Turn on sign-in

Researchers sign in to the Research Portal with an email address and password. Participants sign in to the phone app with their Google account. Turn on both before you register the Android app, so that the app's `google-services.json` file includes the Google sign-in details.

### Step 8: Turn on Email/Password sign-in

In the left-hand menu, open **Security → Authentication** and click **Get started**. On the **Sign-in method** tab, choose **Email/Password**. Switch on **Email/Password**, leave **Email link (passwordless sign-in)** off, and click **Save**.

### Step 9: Turn on Google sign-in

Still on the **Sign-in method** tab, click **Add new provider** and choose **Google**. Switch on **Enable**, then:

- **Public-facing name for project**: participants see this name when they sign in with Google, so use something they'll recognise, such as your study or lab name.
- **Support email for project**: choose an email address from the list. Google requires one.

Click **Save**. If Firebase reminds you to add your app's SHA-1 fingerprint, you can ignore it for now; you'll add it in [Step 19](#fingerprints), once the PRISM installer has created your app's signing key.

## Create the database and file storage

PRISM keeps experiment settings and upload records in a **Cloud Firestore** database, and the uploaded audio and sensor files in **Cloud Storage**. This guide creates both in `australia-southeast1` (Sydney), which PRISM's deployment settings use by default. If you choose another location, the person deploying PRISM must change those settings to match.

### Step 10: Create the Firestore database

In the left-hand menu, open **Databases & Storage → Firestore** and click **Create database**. If you're asked to choose an edition, choose **Standard edition**. Then:

- **Database ID**: leave it as `(default)`. PRISM only uses the default database.
- **Location**: choose `australia-southeast1` (Sydney). It can't be changed later.
- **Security rules**: choose **Start in production mode**. This blocks all access from apps and browsers until PRISM's own security rules are deployed, as described in the [Setup Guide](developer.qmd).

Click **Create**.

### Step 11: Create the Cloud Storage bucket

In the left-hand menu, open **Databases & Storage → Storage** and click **Get started**. Then:

- **Location**: choose `australia-southeast1` (Sydney), the same as Firestore. Firebase may suggest a no-cost US location instead; Sydney uses standard Cloud Storage pricing. The location matters because PRISM's functions that process each upload must run in the bucket's location. Click **Continue**.
- **Security rules**: choose **Start in production mode**, for the same reason as Step 10.

Click **Create**.

## Set up Firebase Hosting

Firebase Hosting gives your project a web address, `<project-id>.web.app` (for example `prism-nat1.web.app`). PRISM publishes the Research Portal there, and participants' invitation links use it to open the phone app.

### Step 12: Get started with Hosting

In the left-hand menu, open **Hosting & Serverless → Hosting** (not **App Hosting**) and click **Get started**. The next screens explain how to install the Firebase command-line tools and deploy a website. You don't need to run any of these commands, since PRISM's deploy script does this for you. Click **Next** on each screen, then **Continue to console**.

## Register the Android app

The PRISM Android app connects to your Firebase project using a `google-services.json` file. You only need to register the app and download this file; the PRISM installer takes care of the rest, so you don't need Android Studio.

### Step 13: Add an Android app

On the project overview, click **+ Add app** and choose **Android**. Enter:

- **Android package name**: a unique identifier for your build of the app, written in reverse-domain format such as `com.yourorg.prism` (this example uses `com.nat.prism`). It can't be changed after you register the app, and the PRISM installer builds the app with this name.
- **App nickname** (optional): a label that only appears in the Firebase Console, such as `PRISM Android`.

Click **Register app**.

![Register the Android app](images/firebase/12-android-register-app.png)

### Step 14: Download `google-services.json`

Click **Download google-services.json** and keep the file somewhere handy, since the PRISM installer will ask for it. Because you turned on Google sign-in in Step 9, the file includes the Google sign-in details the app needs. You'll download it again in [Step 20](#fingerprints), after adding your signing fingerprints. You can ignore the Android Studio instructions. Click **Next**.

![Download google-services.json](images/firebase/13-android-download-config.png)

### Step 15: Skip the SDK setup

The next screen explains how to add the Firebase SDK with Gradle. **Skip these instructions**: the PRISM installer configures the app for you. Click **Next**.

![Firebase SDK instructions (not needed)](images/firebase/14-android-add-sdk.png)

Click **Continue to console**.

![Finish adding the Android app](images/firebase/15-android-next-steps.png)

### Step 16: Find your Android app settings

Your Android app is now listed on the project overview. Click the gear icon (⚙️) on the app card whenever you need its settings, for example to add signing fingerprints, to download `google-services.json` again or to copy its **App ID** (only needed if you distribute the app through Firebase App Distribution).

![The registered Android app](images/firebase/16-overview-android-app.png)

## Register the web app

The PRISM Research Portal signs researchers in through Firebase using your project's **Web API Key**. You get this key by registering a web app.

### Step 17: Add a web app

On the project overview, click **+ Add app** and choose **Web** (`</>`). Enter an **App nickname**; we suggest `prism`, which is the name the [Setup Guide](developer.qmd) uses. Leave **Also set up Firebase Hosting** unticked (you already set up Hosting in Step 12). Click **Register app**.

![Register the web app](images/firebase/17-web-register-app.png)

### Step 18: Copy the Web API Key

Firebase shows a `firebaseConfig` code snippet. Copy the value of **`apiKey`** (a long string beginning with `AIza`) and save it, since the PRISM installer will ask for it. You don't need to run `npm install` or add this code anywhere. Click **Continue to console**.

![Copy the apiKey from the web app config](images/firebase/18-web-app-config.png)

::: {.callout-tip}
You can find the key again at any time under **Settings → General → Your apps → (your web app) → Config**.
:::

## Add the signing fingerprints {#fingerprints}

Do this section during installation, when the PRISM installer shows your app's fingerprints.

Every Android app is signed with a key, and each key has **fingerprints**: short codes that identify it. Firebase needs both of your key's fingerprints:

- **SHA-1**, so participants can sign in to the app with Google.
- **SHA-256**, so participants' invitation links open the PRISM app rather than a web page.

The PRISM installer creates your app's signing key the first time it builds the app, then shows both fingerprints and asks you to add them. Back up the key files the installer names: you need the same key to sign every future version of the app.

### Step 19: Add both fingerprints

Open your Android app's settings (the gear icon on the app card, see Step 16). Under **SHA certificate fingerprints**, click **Add fingerprint**, paste the **SHA-1** value from the installer and click **Save**. Then click **Add fingerprint** again and do the same for the **SHA-256** value.

### Step 20: Download `google-services.json` again

On the same settings page, download `google-services.json` again and give it to the installer as it describes.

::: {.callout-important}
The installer copies settings from `google-services.json` into the app, including the Google sign-in details. Whenever you change sign-in methods or fingerprints, download the file again and re-run the installer, or participants may not be able to sign in.
:::

## Next steps

Your Firebase project is ready. You should now have:

- The `google-services.json` file for your Android app (Step 14).
- Your Web API Key (Step 18).

Continue to the [Setup Guide](developer.qmd), which explains how to generate a **Firebase Service Account Key** and run the PRISM installer. When the installer shows your app's signing fingerprints, come back to [Add the signing fingerprints](#fingerprints).
